source: Real AWS IAM API through AWS CLI; commercial partition
sanitization: Only owned CSV rows retained; root values redacted to field shapes or sentinel values; unrelated user rows discarded. Account and owned names normalized. Passwords, access-key secrets, MFA seeds, private keys, raw CSV/base64/XML and debug logs never retained.

output.Description: No report exists. Starting a new report generation task

limitations: Four-hour cache expiry and expired-report errors were not reached by waiting; documented separately in primary AWS references.

The live report header contains 22 columns and omits additional_credentials_info, although the current primary User Guide lists that column. No claim is made about accounts with more than two keys or certificates per user.

The two owned key pairs are consistent with ascending access-key ID order; the two certificate pairs place inactive before active. These observations do not establish all sorting or tie-breaking rules.
Owned users share one IAM path and appear lexically ordered within it. The complete unrelated account rows are not globally sorted by username; their identities and contents were discarded.

A successful owned STS GetCallerIdentity was followed by GetAccessKeyLastUsed and credential-report values showing no usage yet. This captures propagation lag, not a claim that the call never updates usage.
Password policy, root credentials and root settings were not modified. Password rotation with an account maximum age was not exercised.
Generate returned STARTED and then COMPLETE; INPROGRESS is a documented Generate state but was not observed in this run. Get did return the distinct ReportInProgress error.
